name: Holloway Vale

location.about: A market town of about 70,000 in the Vale of Holloway, fifteen miles down the levels from Westmoor: cheese, wool and gloves, then the creamery and the aircraft factory. Small - but three times champions of England, and twice in the early 1970s.

colours.story: Purple and white - the purple of the glove-makers' dye, the white of the vale's cheese. The club was started in 1870 by the apprentices of the glove works.

rivals.why: the county town fifteen miles up the levels - the county's two clubs, at it since 1883; 61,034 saw Westmoor knock out the champions in the 1972 cup
1972: Northwick took the title Holloway thought was theirs - and in 1931 put eleven past them

history.title: The glovers' club
history.text: Founded in 1870 by apprentices from the glove works. Founders' Cup winners in 1874 - the third final ever played, against Brackenfield. The first Somerset Derby in 1883; champions of England in 1895, ahead of Ashvale.

history.title: Up, down and the cup
history.text: Beaten in the Founders' Cup finals of 1902 and 1905, winners in 1907 (against Fernley). Second Division champions four times - 1907, 1920, 1924 and 1947 - and the Founders' Cup in 1922 and 1948 (Millbrook). An 11-1 at Northwick in 1931 and a 9-0 cup defeat at Lydmouth in 1935 were the low points.

history.title: The great Vale side
history.text: The Founders' Cup in 1960 against Castleford; promoted in 1964; beaten in the 1969 Charter Cup final. Then the side every small town dreams of: champions in 1971 (ahead of Harrowby), second in 1972 behind Northwick - and knocked out of that year's cup at Moorside in front of 61,034 - and champions again in 1973, ahead of Bramhall.

history.title: Back to the vale
history.text: The great side grew old and the aircraft factory closed. Beaten in the 1987 Founders' Cup final; the Founders' Cup in 2002 (against Kingsmere); beaten in the 2009 Charter Cup final. Years in Division 1.

history.title: Knocking on the door
history.text: Up through the play-offs in 2023 (against Morwick), straight back down - and back up as Division 1 champions in 2026, ahead of Harrowby.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1895 = 1894-95).

legends.name: Josiah Coombes
legends.note: Glove-works apprentice; captain of the 1874 cup winners.

legends.name: Roy Chedzoy
legends.note: Two titles in three years with a side that cost almost nothing.

legends.name: Clive Board
legends.note: 663 appearances - the club record; captain in 1971 and 1973.

records.attendance: 38,442 v Westmoor County, League, 1971 (The Paddocks, before seating)

badge.about: A glove, the vale's hill (the tor) and three stars for three titles. Motto 'Manus Juncta' - hands together.
badge.design: A purple shield with a white border. In the centre a white gauntlet glove, palm open; behind it a small white hill with a tower on top. Three small white stars above; 'HOLLOWAY VALE' on a white ribbon below the shield in purple capitals.

ground.name: The Paddocks

stands.name: Glovers Stand
stands.features: the main stand, paid for by the 2002 cup run: tunnel, dugouts, the 1971 and 1973 trophies

stands.name: Market End
stands.features: the home end - on cup days the purple flags reach right down to the pitch

stands.name: Levels Stand
stands.features: a long single tier looking out over the levels

stands.name: Tor End
stands.features: away fans; the oldest stand in the league

ground.surroundings: flat green levels and willow-lined rhynes behind the east stand, a hill with a ruined tower on top beyond the south end, the old glove works and the creamery chimney, a market square with a stone cross
ground.atmosphere: friendly, rural and noisy - a small town that still thinks it's 1973
